casey: FYI: running into a weird hang in the sample-app streaming endpoint. If client cancels early the background streamer task never cleans up and the socket stays open (seen on Py 3.11 + uvicorn). Repro attached.

alex: can you paste a tiny repro or the handler? :thinking_face:

casey: simplified handler:
```
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

async def generator(q):
    try:
        while True:
            item = await q.get()
            yield f"data: {item}\n\n"
    finally:
        print("generator cleanup called")

app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/sse')
async def sse_endpoint(request: Request):
    q = asyncio.Queue()
    # background producer
    task = asyncio.create_task(produce(q))
    return StreamingResponse(generator(q), media_type='text/event-stream')
```
When client disconnects, we expect generator cleanup to run and task to cancel. On our setup the generator finalizer isn't called and the task continues holding references.

katie: interesting — this smells like a lifecycle mismatch between FastAPI/Starlette and async generators. Are you returning an async generator object not awaited? Also which Python runtime (uvicorn workers, loop)?

casey: uvicorn 0.20.0, workers=1, default loop on Windows (no uvloop). Repro runs locally too. Logs show no exception; file descriptors pile up.

simon: can you repro with a synchronous generator wrapped by StreamingResponse? That can change who is responsible for closing. Also check whether the generator object has __anext__ or just __next__.

casey: in our real app some wrappers returned a sync generator from an async function (🤦). That might be the root cause. I attached a minimal repro gist in the ticket.

marie: quick mitigation: explicitly cancel the background task on disconnect via request.is_disconnected check in a loop and call await task.cancel(); also ensure generator implements aclose() and call it from outer scope. But that's awkward for users.

alex: note for SDK folks: our Python SDK doc examples show returning a plain iterator in the sample-streaming snippet — that might encourage this accidental mix. We should clarify examples and maybe add runtime guards that detect sync-gen used in async context and wrap it safely so aclose gets called.

katie: agree. Also file-level type annotations could help catch this: annotate streaming handler return type as AsyncIterator[str] and add a mypy plugin note in docs.

dev-bot: Incident created: INC-9876 (devex-streaming-hang) — assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

casey: filed an SDK issue and sample-app PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps/pull/456 — summary: tighten examples + add a test that simulates client disconnect and asserts generator cleanup. Thanks!

alex: follow-ups: (1) SDK team to add conversion/wrapping guard for sync iterables in async stream APIs, (2) docs update + sample app test, (3) add a small conformance test in CI that runs the disconnect scenario on Windows and Linux. I'll create tracking tickets.

katie: I'll add a unit that calls aclose() via finalizer in CI and fail on leaked tasks. Helps catch regressions.

casey: thanks all — repro gist and logs attached to the ticket. :raised_hands:
